content: Nafcillin may require dosage adjustments and close monitoring for signs of respiratory depression when used in certain scenarios. Below are specific drug interactions and recommendations: 1. Nafcillin and Olutasidenib: Nafcillin reduces the levels and efficacy of olutasidenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 2. Nafcillin and Omadacycline: Omadacycline decreases the effects of nafcillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins, so monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 3. Nafcillin and Omaveloxolone: Nafcillin decreases the levels and effects of omaveloxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Nafcillin and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir/Dasabuvir (DSC): Nafcillin reduces the levels and efficacy of this combination therapy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Nafcillin and Ondansetron: Nafcillin decreases the levels of ondansetron via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, though the clinical significance is unclear. 6. Nafcillin and Osilodrostat: Nafcillin reduces osilodrostat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust osilodrostat dosage if necessary and monitor closely during coadministration or discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers. 7.
